g.aria-label: box st-pressed: PRESSED — rising edge, true for 1 poll
g.text: PRESSED — rising edge, true for 1 poll

g.aria-label: box st-held: HELD — down, steady (repeat timer)
box st-releasing: RELEASING — falling edge, 1 poll
text text-5: still down at next poll
text text-7: still up at next poll

text text-8: PRESSED and RELEASING are true for exactly one poll; UP and HELD persist. A test for 'is it down now' matches PRESSED + HELD. A test for 'was it just pressed' matches PRESSED only. Auto-repeat is a timer on HELD, not a fifth hardware state.
g.text: PRESSED and RELEASING are true for exactly one poll; UP and HELD persist. A test for 'is it down now' matches PRESSED + HELD.
A test for 'was it just pressed' matches PRESSED only. Auto-repeat is a timer on HELD, not a fifth hardware state.

g.aria-label: text text-10: Raw travel, one unsigned byte per trigger. Both triggers are independent — pulling both at once is a legal, ordinary state.
g.text: Raw travel, one unsigned byte per trigger. Both triggers are independent — pulling both at once is a legal, ordinary state.

g.aria-label: box trig-live: LIVE 30–255 — continuous analog travel

box trig-note: A trigger has no rising or falling edge of its own — it reports a level, not an event. XInput treats any raw value under XINPUT_GAMEPAD_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD (30) as released; that comparison is what produces a boolean, and the edge model in panel 2 then applies to THAT derived boolean. Choose the threshold deliberately — a lower one fires sooner but chatters near rest.
g.text: A trigger has no rising or falling edge of its own — it reports a level, not an event. XInput treats any raw value under
XINPUT_GAMEPAD_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD (30) as released; that comparison is what produces a boolean, and the edge model in panel 2
then applies to THAT derived boolean. Choose the threshold deliberately — a lower one fires sooner but chatters near rest.

g.aria-label: box roster-digital: All 16 inputs that run this machine: A / B / X / Y / LB / RB / View / Menu / Guide / Share* / L3 (LS click) / R3 (RS click) / D-Up / D-Down / D-Left / D-Right (* Share exists on Series X|S controllers only)
g.text: All 16 inputs that run this machine: A / B / X / Y / LB / RB / View / Menu / Guide / Share* / L3 (LS click) / R3 (RS click) /
D-Up / D-Down / D-Left / D-Right (* Share exists on Series X|S controllers only)

g.aria-label: box rose-note: Raw axes: LX, LY, RX, RY each report a signed 16-bit value, -32768 to +32767, with +Y up. Radial deadzone constants (XInput): LEFT_THUMB 7849, RIGHT_THUMB 8689 — test the MAGNITUDE, not each axis on its own; per-axis tests carve a square deadzone and cost you the diagonals. The stick is CONTINUOUS: 4-way, 8-way and 16-way are quantisations you impose, normally atan2 binned into equal sectors. Every intermediate angle exists whether or not your code gives it a name. Clicking a stick (L3 / R3) is a separate digital input and runs the panel 2 machine.

g.aria-label: text gl-qcf: QCF 236 — quarter circle forward
text gl-qcb: QCB 214 — quarter circle back
text gl-hcf: HCF 41236 — half circle forward
text gl-hcb: HCB 63214 — half circle back
text gl-dp: DP 623 — dragon punch, Z-motion
text gl-rdp: RDP 421 — reverse dragon punch
text gl-720: 720 — two full spins, either direction
text gl-dbltap: DOUBLE TAP 66 — tap, release, tap
text gl-charge: CHARGE [4]6 — hold back, then forward
text gl-8way: 8-WAY TAP — the base alphabet all of these are built from

text gesture-legend: In every cell up = 8/N and right = 6/E (character facing right). The small digit beside a figure is the numpad direction the motion STARTS from; on DP and RDP the digits 1-2-3 give the order instead.
g.text: In every cell up = 8/N and right = 6/E (character facing right). The small digit beside a figure is the numpad direction the motion STARTS from;
on DP and RDP the digits 1-2-3 give the order instead.

g.aria-label: text hdr-6: 6. COMPLETE INPUT DOMAIN TABLE
text th-4: STATES IT CAN OCCUPY
text t1-1: A, B, X, Y
text t1-3: View, Menu, Guide, Share*
text t1-5: D-Up, D-Down, D-Left, D-Right
text t3-5: 0 or 1 per switch (16 raw combinations)
text t3-7: -32768 to +32767 per axis, +Y is up
text t3-8: -32768 to +32767 per axis, +Y is up
text t4-1: The 4 machine states of panel 2: UP / PRESSED / HELD / RELEASING. Fully independent — any subset of the four may be down together.
g.text: The 4 machine states of panel 2: UP / PRESSED / HELD / RELEASING. Fully independent — any subset of the four may be down together.

g.aria-label: text t4-2: Same 4 machine states. Independent of the trigger sitting behind each one, so LB+LT together is an ordinary state.
g.text: Same 4 machine states. Independent of the trigger sitting behind each one, so LB+LT together is an ordinary state.

g.aria-label: text t4-3: Same 4 machine states. Guide is usually intercepted by the console or OS before your code sees it. * Share: Series X|S only.
g.text: Same 4 machine states. Guide is usually intercepted by the console or OS before your code sees it. * Share: Series X|S only.

g.aria-label: text t4-4: Same 4 machine states, and fully independent of that stick's X/Y — a stick can be clicked at any deflection, including full tilt.
g.text: Same 4 machine states, and fully independent of that stick's X/Y — a stick can be clicked at any deflection, including full tilt.

g.aria-label: text t4-5: 16 raw switch combinations, but 9 meaningful positions: neutral, 4 cardinals, and 4 diagonals formed by holding two switches at once. Opposing pairs are normally rejected by the hardware.
g.text: 16 raw switch combinations, but 9 meaningful positions: neutral, 4 cardinals, and 4 diagonals formed by holding two switches at once.
Opposing pairs are normally rejected by the hardware.

g.aria-label: text t4-6: 256 levels each, so 65 536 pairs. No hardware edge of its own: the boolean is derived by comparing against a threshold (XInput uses 30), and the panel 2 machine then runs on that derived value.
g.text: 256 levels each, so 65 536 pairs. No hardware edge of its own: the boolean is derived by comparing against a threshold (XInput uses
30), and the panel 2 machine then runs on that derived value.

g.aria-label: text t4-7: A continuous plane, 4 294 967 296 raw (x,y) pairs. Radial deadzone below 7849. Every angle and magnitude between the named directions exists whether or not your code bins it.
g.text: A continuous plane, 4 294 967 296 raw (x,y) pairs. Radial deadzone below 7849. Every angle and magnitude between the named directions
exists whether or not your code bins it.

g.aria-label: text t4-8: Same, with a radial deadzone below 8689. The two sticks are wholly independent, so any left-stick state can be combined with any right-stick state.

g.aria-label: box state-space: EVERY CONFIGURATION, COUNTED HONESTLY. Multiply the domains above: 12 freely-combinable digital buttons (2^12) x D-pad (9 legal positions) x triggers (256^2) x sticks (65536^4) = 44,565,841,414,273,689,896,368,472,064 distinct states, about 4.46 x 10^28. Treating all 16 switches as free instead gives exactly 2^96, about 7.92 x 10^28. Neither number can be drawn, and neither needs to be — the controller reports exactly ONE of them per poll. What a map can show, and what input code is actually written against, is the ALPHABET above: each input's own domain, plus the paths traced through it in panel 5.

g.aria-label: box poll-vector: ONE POLL RETURNS ONE ROW. { A B X Y LB RB View Menu Guide Share L3 R3 = 0 or 1 each | D-pad = 4 bits | LT RT = 0 to 255 | LX LY RX RY = -32768 to +32767 } — that row is a single point in the space counted in panel 6, and it is the only thing the hardware ever hands you. Everything in panels 2 and 5 is a statement about how that row CHANGES: an edge is the difference between two consecutive rows, and a gesture is a pattern across a window of them. Neither is a thing you can read out of one poll, which is why input code keeps history.

g.aria-label: text shoulder-note: Shoulder controls sit on the top edge. LT and RT are behind LB and RB and are not visible in this plan view.
g.text: Shoulder controls sit on the top edge. LT and RT are behind LB and RB and are not visible
